title: pvOverlappingCellsDetector
body:
## pvOverlappingCellsDetector

Detects cells that overlap other cells of the same mesh and adds a cell array, NumberOfOverlapsPerCell, counting for each cell how many other cells it collides with (the upstream description's name NumberOfCollisionsPerCell is outdated). Use it as a mesh-quality check, e.g. for overlapping overset regions or badly merged parts; zero everywhere means no overlap was found. It accepts point sets and composite data and works across MPI processes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Tolerance is a length: each cell is shrunk by half of it before testing, so contacts within that margin are ignored; too large a value hides genuine overlaps.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `OverlappingCellsDetector`. Identity: `filters/OverlappingCellsDetector`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

ParaView: This property specifies the input. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet); composite data (multiblock or partitioned collections) (vtkCompositeDataSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet","vtkCompositeDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |

| `Tolerance` | Cells are deflated by 0.5 * Tolerance before the cell overlaps are computed. Deflating is done by translating each cell's faces and edges, in their normal direction, by a vector of norm Tolerance. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
